description: Knowledge of enterprise data inventories, reusable administrative and statistical data assets, metadata-driven discovery, and principles for assessing fitness-for-use across programs.
historic work: Key Activities - Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of divisional statistical programs.
change to work: Long-term strategies will need to incorporate enterprise-wide data asset reuse, digital-first needs identification, and standardized decision gates rather than focusing primarily on divisional program development. Strategy work will increasingly include prioritizing reuse over new collection, embedding auditable needs-assessment processes, and aligning program planning with organization-wide efficiency and automation objectives.
justification: The current element emphasizes program strategy but does not explicitly require enterprise data asset reuse or digital-first governance. The future expectation makes these central to strategy formation.

description: Ability to embed digital platforms, workflow standardization, and automation-readiness criteria into long-term statistical program strategies.
historic work: Key Activities - Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of divisional statistical programs.
change to work: Long-term strategies will need to incorporate enterprise-wide data asset reuse, digital-first needs identification, and standardized decision gates rather than focusing primarily on divisional program development. Strategy work will increasingly include prioritizing reuse over new collection, embedding auditable needs-assessment processes, and aligning program planning with organization-wide efficiency and automation objectives.
justification: The role must move from conventional planning toward digital-first strategic gatekeeping and organization-wide standardization.

description: Ability to lead cross-program behavioural and process change, promote adoption of standardized needs-identification practices, and reinforce digital-first operating models.
historic work: Key Activities - Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of divisional statistical programs.
change to work: Long-term strategies will need to incorporate enterprise-wide data asset reuse, digital-first needs identification, and standardized decision gates rather than focusing primarily on divisional program development. Strategy work will increasingly include prioritizing reuse over new collection, embedding auditable needs-assessment processes, and aligning program planning with organization-wide efficiency and automation objectives.
justification: The update explicitly requires the incumbent to drive culture change toward sustainable, digital production.

description: Ability to evaluate whether proposed collections, processes, or systems are suitable for automation, digital workflow integration, and scalable production.
historic work: Key Activities - Plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes.
change to work: The planning and control function will now begin earlier, at needs identification, requiring formal validation that proposed systems or processes are justified after considering reusable assets, digital workflow compatibility, and automation potential. Control mechanisms will need to include auditable documentation and standardized feasibility review before proceeding to design or implementation.
justification: The future role requires pre-development assessment of automation and workflow compatibility, which is not explicit in the current element.

description: Knowledge of digital intake, tracking, approval, and documentation mechanisms used to govern needs identification and downstream implementation.
historic work: Key Activities - Plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes.
change to work: The planning and control function will now begin earlier, at needs identification, requiring formal validation that proposed systems or processes are justified after considering reusable assets, digital workflow compatibility, and automation potential. Control mechanisms will need to include auditable documentation and standardized feasibility review before proceeding to design or implementation.
justification: Standardized and auditable front-end controls imply stronger procedural and platform-based process governance than currently stated.

description: Knowledge of structured frameworks for evaluating operational feasibility and balancing cost, timeliness, quality, and risk in needs-identification decisions.
historic work: Key Activities - Defines, coordinates and evaluates the cost of statistical system development work.
change to work: Cost evaluation will broaden into a more structured trade-off analysis that weighs cost against timeliness, risk, feasibility, and opportunities for data reuse. The role will increasingly support enterprise resource trade-off decisions rather than only evaluating development costs for a specific system.
justification: The update explicitly adds dynamic cost/timeliness/risk trade-offs and resource optimization requirements beyond current cost evaluation.

description: Ability to compare alternative data acquisition and production approaches using standardized criteria and to justify recommendations transparently.
historic work: Key Activities - Defines, coordinates and evaluates the cost of statistical system development work.
change to work: Cost evaluation will broaden into a more structured trade-off analysis that weighs cost against timeliness, risk, feasibility, and opportunities for data reuse. The role will increasingly support enterprise resource trade-off decisions rather than only evaluating development costs for a specific system.
justification: Participation in resource trade-off decisions requires stronger comparative analysis across options, including reuse versus new collection.

description: Knowledge of AI-enabled discovery tools, metadata search technologies, workflow automation tools, and related opportunities and limitations in statistical operations.
historic work: Key Activities - Identifies and researches trends and developments in mass data processing concepts, methods and techniques.
change to work: Trend research will need to expand beyond general mass processing methods to include digital discovery tools, AI-enabled data asset search and classification, and technologies supporting automation and early needs assessment. The role will be expected to translate these trends into practical governance and investment choices.
justification: The current wording is broad, but the future state specifically requires awareness of digital and AI technologies for discovery and automation.

description: Ability to assess emerging digital tools and convert technical possibilities into operationally feasible and policy-compliant recommendations.
historic work: Key Activities - Identifies and researches trends and developments in mass data processing concepts, methods and techniques.
change to work: Trend research will need to expand beyond general mass processing methods to include digital discovery tools, AI-enabled data asset search and classification, and technologies supporting automation and early needs assessment. The role will be expected to translate these trends into practical governance and investment choices.
justification: The role must connect technology scanning to practical implementation in gatekeeping and process redesign.

description: Ability to engage stakeholders through digital channels at the problem-definition stage, document requirements, and guide them through alternative-data and feasibility discussions.
historic work: Key Activities - Provides expert advisory and consultative services to users within and outside Statistics Canada.
change to work: Advisory services will increasingly focus on challenging or redirecting requests toward reusable assets, lower-burden alternatives, and digitally feasible options. Consultations will need to occur earlier in the process and be supported by documented, platform-enabled evidence about needs, alternatives, costs, and risks.
justification: The update requires earlier and digitally-enabled stakeholder engagement, changing both timing and method of consultation.

description: Knowledge of how to identify, assess, and explain the suitability, limitations, and governance implications of alternative data sources.
historic work: Key Activities - Provides expert advisory and consultative services to users within and outside Statistics Canada.
change to work: Advisory services will increasingly focus on challenging or redirecting requests toward reusable assets, lower-burden alternatives, and digitally feasible options. Consultations will need to occur earlier in the process and be supported by documented, platform-enabled evidence about needs, alternatives, costs, and risks.
justification: The role must be able to advise credibly on reuse and operational feasibility, not only on program outputs and processing.

description: Ability to prepare standardized, traceable proposals that document needs, alternatives considered, decision criteria, feasibility findings, and rationale for recommended action.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 1. Decision making - Prepares program proposals outlining options and recommendations on the statistical framework, strategies, resource implications and impact of new or modified statistical programs.
change to work: Program proposals will need to become more standardized and auditable, explicitly documenting needs assessment, alternative data explorations, asset reuse decisions, cost/timeliness/risk trade-offs, and automation-readiness. Recommendations will need to demonstrate why a proposed initiative is justified relative to existing assets and organizational priorities.
justification: The future requirement for auditable documentation is a direct extension of proposal preparation and is not explicit in the current description.

description: Knowledge of standardized intake, assessment, and documentation practices for needs identification in a digital operating environment.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 1. Decision making - Prepares program proposals outlining options and recommendations on the statistical framework, strategies, resource implications and impact of new or modified statistical programs.
change to work: Program proposals will need to become more standardized and auditable, explicitly documenting needs assessment, alternative data explorations, asset reuse decisions, cost/timeliness/risk trade-offs, and automation-readiness. Recommendations will need to demonstrate why a proposed initiative is justified relative to existing assets and organizational priorities.
justification: The updated proposals must include reuse analysis and digital feasibility assessment, which exceed current expectations.

description: Ability to evaluate and choose among asset reuse, administrative data, integration, model-based approaches, or new collection based on strategic and operational criteria.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 1. Decision making - Determines the methods, concepts, techniques and practices to be applied in the development and operation of statistical programs regarding the acquisition, production and dissemination of data.
change to work: Method determination will shift toward first deciding whether acquisition is needed at all, based on reusable assets and feasible alternatives. The decision space broadens from selecting techniques for production to governing whether and how new work should proceed within digital-first, low-burden, sustainable models.
justification: The updated function requires more than selecting methods; it requires deciding among reuse, integration, and new collection pathways.

description: Knowledge of tools such as data inventories, metadata repositories, cost/risk tracking systems, and digital assessment platforms used to support strategic needs identification.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 1. Decision making - Reviews trends and developments in data processing concepts, methods and techniques in order to present options and recommendations to management on the use and application of new technology to mass data capture, conversion and dissemination applications.
change to work: Recommendations to management will need to cover technologies that support data discovery, needs triage, cost/risk tracking, and automation-readiness, not only downstream capture and dissemination applications.
justification: The future scope extends into front-end digital enablement and enterprise triage technologies.

description: Ability to redesign team practices, set new expectations, align staffing and training, and sustain adoption of standardized digital needs-identification processes.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 2. Leadership and operational management - Manages a unit and leads project teams for special projects. Assesses program requirements and determines objectives and priorities. Plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities, ascertains human resource needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program and project objectives, recruits staff, evaluates employee performance or reviews performance evaluations prepared by subordinates and approves training plans.
change to work: Leadership will increasingly involve embedding standardized needs-identification procedures into unit operations, realigning priorities around enterprise reuse and resource optimization, and building workforce capability in digital tools, alternative data assessment, and auditable decision processes. Team management will also include reinforcing new behavioural expectations and performance standards tied to digital-first practices.
justification: The leadership function must now drive adoption of new enterprise procedures and behaviours, not just manage current operations.

development area: Workforce capability planning for digital operations
description: Knowledge of the competencies required for data asset reuse, digital workflow operation, automation-readiness assessment, and risk-based prioritization.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 2. Leadership and operational management - Manages a unit and leads project teams for special projects. Assesses program requirements and determines objectives and priorities. Plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities, ascertains human resource needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program and project objectives, recruits staff, evaluates employee performance or reviews performance evaluations prepared by subordinates and approves training plans.
change to work: Leadership will increasingly involve embedding standardized needs-identification procedures into unit operations, realigning priorities around enterprise reuse and resource optimization, and building workforce capability in digital tools, alternative data assessment, and auditable decision processes. Team management will also include reinforcing new behavioural expectations and performance standards tied to digital-first practices.
justification: The role must identify and close new workforce capability needs created by digital-first gatekeeping.

description: Ability to allocate and justify resources based on enterprise value, reuse potential, operational risk, and long-term sustainability.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 2. Leadership and operational management - Plans, develops and manages a budget for the unit in accordance with departmental policy and procedures. Exercises direct authority and accountability for allocated funds to meet planned objectives. Authorises, commits and approves expenditures in accordance with approved budgets with the authority to reallocate funds among line objects.
change to work: Budget management will need to place greater emphasis on resource optimization across competing requests, including investments in reusable data assets, digital platforms, and early-stage assessment capacity. The incumbent will need to justify expenditures through formal trade-off analysis rather than mainly within established program envelopes.
justification: The update shifts financial management from unit budgeting toward strategic resource trade-off decisions linked to digital enablement and reuse.

development area: Strategic client advisory for problem framing
description: Ability to help stakeholders clarify needs, assess alternatives, and accept evidence-based trade-offs involving scope, timeliness, burden, and feasibility.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 3. Communication - Provides expert advisory and consultative services to policy makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academia.
change to work: The advisory role will evolve from explaining program findings and methods toward shaping demand, framing feasible options, and guiding clients toward reusable or lower-burden approaches. This includes documenting needs and constraints through structured digital engagement methods.
justification: The future role requires more consultative challenge and co-design at the problem-definition stage.

description: Ability to convene stakeholders across programs, broker consensus on shared standards, and resolve competing interests in data reuse and resource allocation.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 3. Communication - Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop understanding, consensus and share knowledge of the program area.
change to work: These forums will increasingly be used to negotiate cross-program data asset reuse, establish common needs-identification procedures, and build consensus on enterprise standards for digital gatekeeping and resource prioritization.
justification: Cross-program coordination becomes more central because the update requires enterprise-wide data asset utilization and standardized procedures.

description: Knowledge of data catalogues, metadata standards, searchable inventories, and platform capabilities that support locating and assessing reusable data assets.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 4. Knowledge of specialized fields - Advanced knowledge of systems analysis and design and of new and emerging computer technology and applications in order to establish and manage mass statistical data collection, production and dissemination environments.
change to work: This knowledge base will need to extend from production systems into digital discovery, metadata platforms, workflow orchestration, and AI-enabled support for front-end needs assessment and asset identification.
justification: Current systems knowledge is oriented to collection, production, and dissemination; the update adds front-end digital platforms and AI-enabled discovery.

description: Knowledge of how AI can support discovery, triage, classification, and automation in needs identification, alongside associated risks and controls.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 4. Knowledge of specialized fields - Advanced knowledge of systems analysis and design and of new and emerging computer technology and applications in order to establish and manage mass statistical data collection, production and dissemination environments.
change to work: This knowledge base will need to extend from production systems into digital discovery, metadata platforms, workflow orchestration, and AI-enabled support for front-end needs assessment and asset identification.
justification: AI awareness is explicitly identified in the update and is not directly present in the current specialized knowledge.

description: Knowledge of intake governance, stage-gating, prioritization models, and enterprise oversight practices for approving or redirecting statistical initiatives.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 4. Knowledge of specialized fields - Knowledge of the principles and practices of project management including the management of human and financial resources.
change to work: Project management knowledge will need to be supplemented by portfolio-style governance at the intake stage, where comparative prioritization, auditable gating, and enterprise trade-offs are made before projects are launched.
justification: The revised phase functions as a gatekeeper and requires broader intake and portfolio governance than traditional project management alone.

description: Knowledge of available data assets across programs, including access conditions, metadata quality, reuse constraints, and typical use cases.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 5. Contextual knowledge - Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances and to recommend changes to other statistical programs.
change to work: Cross-program knowledge becomes more central and must be broadened from awareness of related programs to systematic understanding of enterprise data holdings and their reusability for emerging needs before new collection is pursued.
justification: The update elevates cross-program asset utilization from useful context to a required first step in needs identification.

description: Ability to convert stakeholder requests into feasible statistical service options that reflect available assets, production constraints, and standardized assessment criteria.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 5. Contextual knowledge - Knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide expert advice on program results.
change to work: Understanding users will need to include their digital engagement expectations, tolerance for trade-offs, and openness to alternative products or reused data sources. The role will increasingly interpret user needs in operationally feasible and sustainable terms.
justification: The updated role requires translating client demand into standardized, digitally assessed options rather than primarily identifying needs and markets.

description: Ability to assess whether existing frameworks, processes, and data assets can be adapted or reused to meet new needs more efficiently than launching new activity.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 6. Research and analysis - Reviews the conceptual framework of existing statistical programs and determines the need for development, modification and adaption.
change to work: This review will need to be more explicitly comparative and evidence-based, asking whether existing programs or assets can satisfy a need through reuse, adaptation, or integration before recommending new development. The conceptual review becomes part of a formal gatekeeping process.
justification: The updated function requires more rigorous comparative assessment across existing assets and new proposals.

description: Ability to evaluate implementation practicality, sustainability, digital compatibility, and organizational impacts of proposed data acquisition or processing approaches.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 6. Research and analysis - Assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and the associated costs and limitations and identifies the availability and reliability of new data sources to evaluate the suitability of new hardware and software and to determine the short and long term program impact and benefits.
change to work: Assessment activity will expand to include formal evaluation of alternative data availability, discovery tools, automation options, and risk-based operational feasibility. The analysis will need to support auditable intake decisions and enterprise optimization, not only program-specific method selection.
justification: The current element addresses costs and limitations, but the future state requires broader operational feasibility and auditable option assessment.

description: Ability to assess requests through standardized digital processes that capture needs, test against available assets and capacities, and record decision rationale.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts - 6. Research and analysis - Investigates client requirements for statistical information and determines the capacity and ability of existing or modified systems to meet these requirements.
change to work: Client requirement analysis will occur earlier and will require explicit examination of whether existing data assets, systems, or workflows can satisfy the need, alongside documented trade-offs if they cannot. Capacity analysis becomes part of a digital intake and triage process.
justification: The revised process requires structured intake and triage rather than more informal client requirement analysis alone.

description: Knowledge of how shared digital platforms support stakeholder intake, needs tracking, commitments management, and transparent prioritization across statistical programs.
historic work: Key Activities - Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of divisional statistical programs.
change to work: Long-term strategy will need to incorporate platform-enabled consultation, reuse-first service design, measurable prioritization criteria, and explicit decision governance. The activity shifts from general strategic planning toward stewardship of a transparent, evidence-based intake and prioritization model for program development.
justification: The current wording emphasizes strategic planning for statistical programs but does not explicitly require stewardship of digital consultation ecosystems, evidence-based intake governance, or reuse-first prioritization.

description: Ability to align program choices with resource constraints, reuse opportunities, automation potential, and agency-wide priorities using defensible decision criteria.
historic work: Key Activities - Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of divisional statistical programs.
change to work: Long-term strategy will need to incorporate platform-enabled consultation, reuse-first service design, measurable prioritization criteria, and explicit decision governance. The activity shifts from general strategic planning toward stewardship of a transparent, evidence-based intake and prioritization model for program development.
justification: Future strategy decisions require formal balancing of demand, feasibility, resource availability, and reuse potential, which is not explicitly developed in the current work-description.
